results.title: Kendrapara Gajalaxmi Puja begins, recalling Goddess Lakshmi’s emergence during Samudra Manthan
results.description: The famous Gajalaxmi Puja of Kendrapara has begun, bringing the town alive with festive fervour as devotees gather to worship Goddess Lakshmi. Decorative arches, colourful illuminations and beautifully adorned pandals have transformed the town, drawing large crowds from the first day of the seven-day celebration. The festival is being observed at 68 puja pandals across Kendrapara town and more than 100 pandals in the surrounding areas this year. Among the major attractions is the Ganga Bhagirathi Puja Mandap at Madhial, where Goddess Lakshmi is adorned with a gold crown and a magnificent silver backdrop. The festival also brings families and relatives together, with many people looking forward to visiting the pandals throughout the week. A devotee said, “We eagerly wait for Gajalaxmi Puja every year. Our relatives come to visit, and we spend all seven days enjoying the celebrations and visiting different pandals. The arrival of the Goddess fills the entire town with happiness, and we believe her blessings make these days especially joyful.” Why Is Gajalaxmi Puja Celebrated? According to a priest, the festival is associated with the appearance of Goddess Lakshmi during the churning of the cosmic ocean, known as Samudra Manthan in Hindu mythology. “According to tradition, Goddess Lakshmi emerged during the churning of the ocean. Her appearance is associated with the full moon day of the Hindu month of Ashwin, which is observed as an auspicious occasion to worship her. Devotees across the country offer prayers to the Goddess, seeking prosperity, wealth and well-being,” the priest said. Elaborate Security Arrangements In Kendrapara Meanwhile, the district administration has made extensive arrangements to ensure that the celebrations are held peacefully. Around 25 platoons of police personnel have been deployed at various locations across Kendrapara town, while CCTV cameras are keeping watch over sensitive areas. On the other hand, Dhenkanal is also bustling with religious fervour and festivities, where Goddess Lakshmi is being worshipped at 41 puja pandals.
